title: How Did Birds Outlive the Other Dinosaurs? - Nautilus
gist: A Current Biology paper by US and Chinese paleontologists uses a theropod coprolite from Montana containing perfectly preserved feathers, fish scales and leg bones to explain why birds were the only dinosaur group to survive the asteroid impact 66 million years ago.

insights.claim: When an asteroid struck Earth 66 million years ago, spewing dust clouds and creating hellish conditions, all the large dinosaurs perished while birds were the only dinosaur group to make it through.
insights.so_what: The canonical case study of selective extinction survival: body size and diet, not lineage prestige, determined who passed through the bottleneck.
insights.locator: When an asteroid collided with Earth 66 million years ago
insights.speaker: Devin Reese

insights.claim: A paper published in Current Biology by paleontologists from the U.S. and China reports evidence for why birds alone among dinosaurs survived the end-Cretaceous extinction.
insights.so_what: US-China co-authorship remains the norm in vertebrate paleontology, a field where Chinese fossil sites dominate supply.
insights.locator: A paper published today in the journal Current Biology
insights.speaker: Devin Reese

insights.claim: The hypothesis rests on a fossilized theropod dinosaur dropping (coprolite) found in Montana that contained tiny, perfectly preserved feathers, fish scales and leg bones.
insights.so_what: Coprolites preserve soft tissue that ordinary fossilization destroys, making them disproportionately information-rich relative to their obscurity.
insights.quote: Inside the poop were tiny, perfectly preserved feathers, fish scales, and leg bones, which provided critical clues in the story of bird survival.
insights.locator: Paleontologists from the U.S. and China formed a hypothesis
insights.speaker: Devin Reese
